1. PROFILE_DEFINITION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Facts that define the cluster itself. These variables and diagnostics produced the
cluster; they are NOT re-tested as post-cluster findings (doing so would be circular).

Branch: G — strict final-path analytical cohort n=56 (of 362 total strict-cohort respondents: D=191, E=34, F=81, G=56).
Retained dimension: Household economic role and dependency
Number of profiles in this retained model (k): 2
This profile's id and label: Profile 2 — "Predominantly self-income provider/contributor"
This profile's exact frozen size: n=15 (cross-verified against the Part III freeze-verification table in the source report)

Exact cluster-forming variables (the only inputs used to build this clustering; all
other survey variables were deliberately excluded from distance calculation and are
only used descriptively in sections 2-3 below):
  - household_income
  - household_size
  - household_unemployed
  - household_workers
  - primary_earner_status
  - primary_income_source

Theoretical basis and purpose: Household economic role/dependency position (Bourdieu economic capital / ILO SWTS household framework).

Clustering method: Gower distance over original mixed-type responses (no invented 0-100
scores), consensus of repeated K-medoids and spectral clustering across 100 matched
80% subsamples (200 base partitions), final clusters from K-medoids on (1 - co-association).

Validation diagnostics for this retained model: Gower silhouette 0.372; bootstrap/subsample ARI 1.000; source-method ARIs 0.854 and 0.718; permutation p=0.012; 9 of 9 mandatory validation checks passed.
Final decision status: Retained narrowly; describes role/dependency, not resource level.
Model-level caution (from the frozen decision register): This is an economic-role/dependency pattern, not a low-versus-high household-resource classification.

Additional definitional context: The original working title implied household resource LEVEL, but structural household-resource variables alone had ARI -0.016 with the final grouping — resource level does not explain this partition. Primary income source was the strongest single item, though no single item alone exactly reproduced membership. The defensible interpretation is therefore economic ROLE/DEPENDENCY (whether the respondent is a provider/contributor vs. supported by family/partner), not household wealth.

Interpretation of this specific profile (verbatim from the frozen report's per-model
profile table):
  86.7% were main/shared earners; 66.7% reported a regular job/business as their main personal income source.

Reminder: this profile exists only WITHIN this one retained dimension. A respondent's
membership here says nothing about their membership in any other branch's or dimension's
profile system (see PROHIBITED_INFERENCES).

4. CAUTIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Model-level caution: This is an economic-role/dependency pattern, not a low-versus-high household-resource classification.
Additional model context: The original working title implied household resource LEVEL, but structural household-resource variables alone had ARI -0.016 with the final grouping — resource level does not explain this partition. Primary income source was the strongest single item, though no single item alone exactly reproduced membership. The defensible interpretation is therefore economic ROLE/DEPENDENCY (whether the respondent is a provider/contributor vs. supported by family/partner), not household wealth.
FDR-correction context: Among the findings that passed the effect-size/coverage reporting screen for this model, 0 of 8 remained significant after FDR correction. All reported findings for this profile are descriptive/exploratory evidence only.

Profile-specific caution (verbatim from the frozen evidence summary): This is an economic-role/dependency pattern, not a low-versus-high household-resource classification. Small profile (n=15). Some categorical comparisons contain sparse cells. None of the selected comparisons remained below FDR 0.05; effect sizes are descriptive evidence.

Small-profile caution: this profile's size (n=15) is small; percentages within it are more sensitive to individual respondents and less stable than in larger profiles.

Conditional-denominator caution: 4 of 30 variables tested against this model are conditional (asked only of an eligible subgroup via survey routing, e.g. only active jobseekers, only those who worked while studying). Their percentages use the eligible-subgroup denominator shown in section 3, not the full profile size. A blank caused by survey routing was never treated as a 'No' answer during profiling.

Cross-dimensional caution: the following variables tested against this model also form part of another retained clustering model; their relationship to this profile is descriptive only and is NOT independent statistical validation of this model:
  - Ever worked for pay/profit: Forms the separate G engagement model.
  - Wants further education/training: Forms the separate G engagement model.
  - District: Many district categories can create sparse tables.
  - Reason not currently in labour force: Forms the separate G engagement model.
  - Wants to work in future: Forms the separate G engagement model.

Sparse-cell caution: 19 of 30 variables tested against this model contain sparse expected-cell counts (categorical tables with rare category combinations); percentages built from sparse tables are listed in section 3 and should be read with extra caution, especially for high-cardinality variables such as district, sector or stated obstacle.

General measurement cautions (apply to every profile in this knowledge base):
  - A reported percentage is a within-profile percentage in this 362-respondent strict
    cohort, not a population estimate for all Sri Lankan youth.
  - Effect sizes rank descriptive differences; they do not prove that cluster membership
    caused the characteristic.
  - Consensus clustering stability shows reproducibility under the specified procedure;
    it does not prove a natural, causal, or permanent youth type.
  - Profile names are descriptive and must not stigmatise respondents or be used to deny
    programme access.

5. PROHIBITED_INFERENCES

Universal (applies to all 17 retained profiles):

  - Do not treat profile membership as a diagnosis, permanent trait, or whole-person label. Profiles are exploratory response-pattern groups within ONE retained dimension only. The same respondent can simultaneously belong to different profiles across different retained dimensions (for example a Branch D respondent has independent motivation, economic and educational-trajectory profile memberships) — no single profile describes the whole person.

  - Do not treat effect sizes or association strength as evidence of causation. A reported association (e.g. 'Profile A more often reported X') describes a measured difference in this sample; it does not establish that being in Profile A caused X, or that X caused profile membership.
  - Do not treat a finding that did not pass this model's effect-size/coverage reporting screen (see DIRECT_GROUP_DISTRIBUTIONS) as an approved or reportable difference. Untagged distributions are raw descriptive data only, not vetted findings.
  - Do not treat a finding as statistically confirmed population evidence merely because it appears here. Most models in this knowledge base have few or zero findings that remain significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (see this profile's CAUTIONS section and fdr_note) — effect sizes are the primary ranking evidence, and p-values (raw or adjusted) are supporting evidence only.

Course/programme recommendation requires a separate, transparent, expert-reviewed matching stage that combines this profile information with the individual's own stated preferences, eligibility and the structured NYSC course catalogue.
